# briefs/

One Markdown file per day, named `YYYY-MM-DD.md`. Each brief is the canonical operational output of the daily routine. Once committed, briefs are treated as historical record — corrections happen via a follow-up commit on the next brief, not by editing past files.

## File contents (canonical structure — v2 schema, prompt v2.23+)

```
# CTI Daily Brief — YYYY-MM-DD

> AI-generated content notice
**Generated by:** {model} ({model-id}) · **Audience:** SOC Tier 2/3, IR, Threat Hunting · **Classification:** TLP:CLEAR · **Language:** English · **Prompt:** v{N.M}

## 0. TL;DR
## 1. Immediate Actions                                  (often absent — see below)
## 2. Active Threats, Trending Actors, Notable Incidents & Disclosures
## 3. Trending Vulnerabilities                           (consolidated, with inclusion gates)
## 4. Research & Investigative Reporting
## 5. Updates to Prior Coverage
## 6. Deep Dive — {topic}
## 7. Action Items                                       (derived from today's content only)
## 8. Verification Notes
```

§ 1 (Immediate Actions) is **omitted entirely** on most days — render only
when at least one item meets the bar (actively-exploited zero-day with
RCE/auth-bypass; zero-click RCE; pre-auth RCE on internet-exposed enterprise
software; supply-chain compromise of widely deployed software; active
campaign with confirmed European public-sector impact).

§ 2 (Active Threats / Incidents) is the consolidated section that absorbs
what earlier prompt versions split between Active Threats / Switzerland,
Europe & Public Sector / Notable Incidents & Disclosures. The CH / EU /
public-sector emphasis rides on the per-item region + sector tags in the
metadata footer (see below); items with that nexus are ordered first.

§ 3 (Trending Vulnerabilities) consolidates all CVE-centric coverage. The
inclusion gate is explicit: CISA KEV, ENISA EUVD `exploited=true`, ENISA
EUVD CVSS ≥9.0, vendor / HIGH-reliability ITW report, or pre-auth
internet-exposed RCE with public PoC. CVEs that don't clear a gate stay
out of the brief and are logged in § 8 with the reason.

The `**Prompt:** v{N.M}` field references the matching entry in
[`../prompts/CHANGELOG.md`](../prompts/CHANGELOG.md); the site renders it
as a clickable badge so a reader can tell at a glance which editorial-policy
version produced the brief.

The full structure and per-section conventions are defined in
[`../prompts/daily-cti-brief.md`](../prompts/daily-cti-brief.md), Phase 4.

## Per-item metadata footer (NORMATIVE — added in v2.23)

Every individual content block in §§ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 ends with **exactly
one italic Markdown line** at the end of the block:

```
— *Source: [Title](URL) [· Additional source: [Title](URL)] · Tags: tag1, tag2 · Region: region1[, region2] [· CVE: CVE-…] [· CVSS: …] [· Vector: …] [· Auth: …] [· Status: …]*
```

Field separator is the middle dot ` · ` (U+00B7 with surrounding spaces).
Controlled vocabularies live in [`../site/taxonomy.yaml`](../site/taxonomy.yaml);
the build refuses any item using a value not in the taxonomy. The build
parses the footer to:

- emit a stable `/items/<slug>/` page per content block,
- populate `/tags/<tag>/` and `/regions/<region>/` index pages,
- emit one entry in `feed-items.xml` (the per-item RSS feed),
- render a structured "Sources / Region / Tags / CVE / CVSS / Vector / Auth /
  Status" badge block under each item on the published page.

`Source` is always the most primary source the agent could verify (vendor
advisory > national CERT/CSIRT > MITRE/NVD > ENISA EUVD > researcher write-up
> aggregator). When only an aggregator was reachable, the item is flagged in
§ 8 as `included with reduced confidence: only aggregator source available`.

## Rules

- **Inline links only.** Every claim is followed by `([Publisher, YYYY-MM-DD](URL))` immediately. There is no bibliography section.
- **No IOCs.** No file hashes, no IP addresses, no attacker domains/URLs, no detection rule code.
- **No vanity metrics.** No dwell time, breakout time, %-YoY counts, "X new adversaries tracked", "$Y billion in damage".
- **Empty-section discipline.** Sections with no qualifying items state so explicitly (e.g., `*No CVEs cleared the inclusion gates in this window.*`). § 1 is the exception — omit it entirely on quiet days.
- **Updates only when material.** Items from the last 7 briefs do not reappear unless under § 5 with a delta, the original date, and a metadata footer.
- **Source dates** appear inside the link text (`[Publisher, 2026-05-04](...)`), so a reader can judge recency without clicking.
- **Metadata footer on every item.** Missing or malformed footer on a post-cut-over brief is a build failure.

## AI-generated content

Every brief in this directory is autonomously generated by an LLM running as a Claude Code routine on Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure, executing the prompts in [`../prompts/`](../prompts/). The exact model varies with the routine's runtime configuration; each brief opens with an AI-generation notice and a `Generated by:` metadata line where the model identifies itself by name and ID. Verify against linked primary sources before acting on operationally critical claims.

## First run

The repository ships with no briefs. The first daily routine run will create `YYYY-MM-DD.md`; the first weekly routine run will create `weekly/YYYY-Www.md`.
